summary: You can build and install in your own workspace right away, and public distribution to other workspaces does not need a Marketplace listing. Listing in the Slack Marketplace is a separate review that Slack estimates at up to 10 weeks for new apps.

verdict.label: Self-serve to start, review to list
verdict.effort: Not measured. Creating and installing is quick; the Marketplace path adds a checklist, testing on a separate workspace and a long review.
verdict.wait: None for public distribution. Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (Slack's estimates, not guarantees).
verdict.reason: Activating public distribution lets other workspaces install your app without a Marketplace listing. Slack recommends a Marketplace listing for commercial apps, and that review has long published timelines.

steps.title: Create an app
steps.detail: Go to the Slack API apps page and choose Create New App, from scratch.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs
steps.detail: In the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions, add your redirect URL. It must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor (#). The redirect_uri you send during install must match it or be a subdirectory of it.

steps.title: Add bot and user scopes
steps.detail: Bot scopes are for your app's bot user. Request user scopes only if the app must act on behalf of a user. Pick only what you need. An agent can map actions like 'post a message' to scopes.

steps.title: Install to your own workspace
steps.detail: Install it and copy the tokens to test the flow.

steps.title: Turn on public distribution
steps.detail: In your app's dashboard, open Manage Distribution, find Share Your App with Other Workspaces, complete the checklist and click Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL. Your OAuth redirect, interaction request, options load and Events API request URLs must support SSL.

steps.title: Optional: submit to the Marketplace
steps.detail: Not required to let other workspaces install, but Slack recommends it for commercial apps. Test on a workspace that is not your development workspace, from install through uninstall. Your app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces. Provide test account credentials and a way for reviewers to install the app, since they cannot access any workspace. A short demo video is recommended and speeds review.

blockers.title: Marketplace review is slow
blockers.detail: Slack estimates a preliminary review of up to 10 business days, then a functional review of up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes. All feedback must be addressed before listing, and your queue place resets on each resubmission during the preliminary review. Reviews cannot be accelerated.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit with clear testing instructions and a short demo video. Meanwhile, share your public distribution install link with early customers.

blockers.title: Marketplace needs 10 active workspaces
blockers.detail: Your app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces, meaning used in the past 28 days, before you submit.
blockers.what_to_do: Use public distribution to pilot with early customers first. Plan the listing as a later step, not a launch blocker.

blockers.title: Workspace admin approval
blockers.detail: Admins can turn on an Approve apps setting. When it is on, a Slack user must request the app and an admin must approve it before it is installed for the team to use.
blockers.what_to_do: Give users a short message they can send to their admin explaining the scopes.
